newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico ends special prosecutor role in key killings.
newsitem.headline: Mexico ends special prosecutor role in key killings.

text.p: Mexico's Attorney General's Office (PRR) said on Thursday it had dissolved the office of special prosecutor in two high-profile assassinations, placing the cases in the hands of an assistant attorney general.

Attorney General Jorge Madrazo transferred investigations of the murders of a top ruling-party politician and a Roman Catholic cardinal from the office of a fired special prosecutor to a new assistant attorney general, Jose Luis Ramos Rivera.

Ramos "will have the responsibility to continue, advance and deepen the investigations into the homicides of Cardinal Juan Jesus Posadas Ocampo and Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu," a PGR statement said. "The prior special prosecution is dissolved."

The previous special prosecutor in both cases, Pablo Chapa Benzanilla, was fired when Madrazo's predecessor as attorney general, Antonio Lozano, was dismissed by President Ernesto Zedillo in December.
Ramos, who was named to his post along with a host of others forming Madrazo's new team, has thus been handed responsibility over two of the most explosive unresolved cases in Mexico.

In one, the brother of disgraced former President Carlos Salinas de Gortari is accused of masterminding the 1994 murder of Ruiz Massieu, who was secretary general of the long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI).
Raul Salinas de Gortari, the former president's brother, remains in a high-security prison awaiting a resolution of the case.

The new assistant attorney general also takes over control of the probe into the 1993 murder of Posadas, who was gunned down in his car at the airport in Guadalajara, Mexico's second-largest city, allegedly by drug traffickers.
Authorities have said Posadas was a victim of mistaken identity but the Catholic Church remains sceptical of that version, suspecting Posadas was deliberately murdered.
At least two men have been arrested in the case, believed to have been hired by the feared Arellano Felix brothers, who run the massive Pacific drug cartel based in Tijuana, Mexico.
